control_action: render a graph response whose mode field is absent
observed_behavior: The graph shell resolves mode from controller state, but projection controls and node semantics read only response.data.mode. When a valid response omits that redundant field, full-map state exposes flow/orbit controls that cannot change the deterministic full-map layout.
expected_behavior: Every graph subrenderer uses one effective mode resolved from response mode or the authoritative controller request/state, so visible controls always affect the rendered layout.
operational_impact: The UI can display nonfunctional layout controls and incorrect coverage/selection labels, making the Knowledge Graph appear interactive while ignoring those actions.

discovery_evidence.claim: The flow control rendered unpressed while controller state was full/community after search.
Projection branches repeatedly on data.mode while the shell separately resolves state.graphMode.

next_action: Resolve effective mode once inside projection and use it for layout controls, coverage, interactions, scene identity, and labels; exercise a focused analysis mode before testing orbit/flow controls.

display.detail: Projection shows controls for the wrong effective mode.

user_edit_action.detail: Layout buttons accept clicks but full-map layout ignores them.

input_validation.detail: No shared effective-mode invariant guards the response/state mismatch.

runtime_effect.detail: Graph renders but exposed layout action can be ineffective.

result_acknowledgement.detail: Response is accepted without reconciling omitted mode.

failure_handling.detail: Omitted redundant mode silently creates divergent semantics.

recovery_rollback.detail: No visible recovery identifies the ineffective control.
